- When sentiment is negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is positive but model forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–7 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to short-term forecast to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model often lags true price by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias to capture sentiment-driven acceleration.
